newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Reuters Poll Trend for Australian politics - May 9.
newsitem.headline: Reuters Poll Trend for Australian politics - May 9.

text.p: The Australian government's opinion poll lead has crashed in the past couple of months, from the 12 percentage points typical since December to only around six points last weekend, the Reuters Poll Trend shows.

Both of the major blocs are losing support. Primary support for the ruling Liberal-National coalition is down eight or more points since a recent peak in March while the Labor opposition has lost one or two points in that time.
No trend estimates are yet available for the One Nation Party of independent MP Pauline Hanson.
But a simple average of recent polls suggests the populist MP, who opposes aboriginal welfare and Asian immigration, has the support of roughly 10 percent of voters.

On Tuesday, we calculated a primary-vote gap between the major blocs of four percentage points, a figure that was reported by the Australian Broadcasting Corp. Since then, however, a Morgan poll has been published, showing a larger gap than in the other two. So we have revised our estimates.
